summary.text: Charles Tran is the Liberal candidate for Mulgrave at the 2026 Victorian election. The son of Vietnamese refugees, he has taught in secondary schools for 18 years. His party profile says he also volunteers as a firefighter, leads a Scout group and belongs to Rotary, and the ABC adds that he volunteers for St John Ambulance as a first responder.

priorities.text: Lower living costs for Mulgrave households
Better health services
Safer streets, buses and trains, backed by the party's pledge of 3000 more police and 200 more PSOs
Good-quality education and health care for every family

sources.title: Mulgrave: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Charles Tran, Liberal for Mulgrave, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Cody Rebbechi is One Nation's candidate for Mulgrave at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC, his working life has taken in logistics, retail, hospitality management, repairs and disability support, and he and his wife have rented in Springvale since 2018. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

occupation.text: Logistics, retail, hospitality management, repair and disability support work

sources.title: Mulgrave: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Connor Buchanan is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Mulgrave at the 2026 Victorian election. He works as a maintenance fitter and belongs to the Australian Manufacturing Workers' Union (AMWU). His party page says he rents, grew up in Melbourne's south-east, and has been active in workplace organising and in protests over Gaza, the far right, trans rights and discrimination against First Nations people.

priorities.text: I stand for a socialist society
Shifting wealth gains away from the very rich
Ending racism, sexism, homophobia, transphobia and other bigotry
Housing and health care everyone can afford, without choosing between rent and a GP visit

sources.title: Mulgrave: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Connor Buchanan, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Eden Foster is the Labor MP for Mulgrave, elected at the November 2023 by-election that followed Daniel Andrews' resignation. Before that she was a Greater Dandenong councillor from 2020 and the city's mayor from 2022. She is running again in Mulgrave in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Psychologist at a North Melbourne Catholic school

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia doesn't say what label she stood under at this council election; the code is her party membership.

sources.title: Eden Foster, Parliament of Victoria
Eden Foster, Wikipedia

summary.text: Fotini Theodossopoulou is the Libertarian candidate for Mulgrave at the 2026 Victorian election. Her party profile says her career has been in sales and marketing, including senior roles at a large media company, and that she now manages a family-owned outdoor construction business. She contested Mulgrave as an independent at the 2022 state election.

occupation.text: Manager of a family-owned outdoor construction business

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia names this candidate Tina Theodossopoulou, described as the 2022 Mulgrave candidate; no source confirms it is the same person.

priorities.text: Smaller government, to cut corruption and waste
Less red tape, including for small residential building projects
A Bill of Rights protecting free speech and personal choice
Support for local small and medium-sized businesses
Restoring safety and security in her community

summary.text: Ian Cook is standing as an independent for Mulgrave at the 2026 Victorian election, his third run for the seat. He spent more than 30 years running I Cook Foods, a Dandenong catering business that was shut in 2019 during a listeria investigation; the ABC notes that a court later found the business had been denied procedural fairness. In both of his earlier Mulgrave contests, at the general election of 2022 and the by-election a year later, he came second after preferences.

occupation.text: Businessman, former owner of I Cook Foods

priorities.text: Lower grocery, energy and water bills by cutting state taxes and charges
Halving stamp duty and scrapping land tax on homes offered for rent
Road repairs and fixing known danger spots, including traffic lights at Police Road, Albany Drive and Smith Road
Tougher bail, more police and a 24-hour Springvale police station
A 'Ryan's Law' doubling penalties for politicians or police who abuse their position

summary.text: Paul J Schofield is the Greens candidate for Mulgrave at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC describes him as working in marketing, and he says he has lived in ten cities across the UK, Australia and the United States. On his party page he describes his politics as social democratic and environmentalist, and says that as a Green he is not funded by corporate or lobby-group donors.

priorities.text: Public education, especially adult migrant education, TAFE and universities
Public health, with a particular interest in dental care
Community sport and fitness, all forms of transport, and the arts
Pressing Labor to work with the Greens if the parliament is hung
Keeping politics free of corporate and lobby-group donations

sources.title: Mulgrave: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Paul Schofield, Candidate for Mulgrave, Victorian Greens

summary.text: Stewart Dobrzynski is the Family First candidate for Mulgrave at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party profile says he started in IT as a support engineer in 1994 and has led IT teams as a manager for the past 18 years, and that he has lived in Melbourne's outer east for more than 50 years. He is involved with his church, a school board and a Little Athletics committee, and the party says he won silver in track and field at the 2026 Masters World Championships.

priorities.text: Reining in state government spending
Relief for families from cost-of-living pressure
Safer local streets and less crime and violence
More accountability in government
